title: Adding QoL Updates to Older games.
author: Xenobyte_VT
selftext: Recently I've started playing through my old library of games from franchises that have long since had many QoL updates over the years (I.e Pokemon with shared party exp and catching experience, or Digimon with being able to have full box and digi lab access in game menu). So I've begun to test AI to see if I could add these QoL improvements to these old games and I've had some success and I'm beginning to question is this ethical or even appropriate to do?

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body:
If anything involves copyright or IP, I think it's fine to edit, if you just do on your own computer to see if you can. 

But if one is modifying something and then putting it back out there, it would need to have no, expired, or MIT some kind of license that says "yes you may change this and post it or even sell it."

That being said, when Zork's original code was released under MIT license. Since it was such an obtuse and crazy hard game (to little kid me) I wanted to revisit it and make some changes.

I was able to compile the original ZIL code and then feature by feature translate into a modern "text-adventure" language known as Inform 7. 

Now I have Zork working in a modern language I know (and can vibe code in easily). The goal is to play with the idea of bringing modern QoL game ideas to old obtuse games. I could have worked in the original ZIL too if I wanted to fully vibe code it, but that language had the limitations that made the QoL features missing.

Sometimes people want and love the older, harder, style of games. I think it's fine to want to make them more accessible to more people. 

I've corrected all its known bugs, added more flavor and hint text, and given it some color and sound. 

[My progress so far.](https://johnesco.github.io/zork1/)
